$comment: The canonical model-routing catalog for unattended work.
One task gets one effort tier. A tier names the implementer model and the
independent reviewer model, and both are pinned provider model IDs. A
family name such as "Sonnet" is a display name for an operator. It is
never what a run resolves to.
The markers are L, S and H, for Lightweight, Standard and Hard. They
describe the execution effort that was selected. They do not describe the
estimated size of a ticket.
lib/agentqueue/effort.py loads this file, and docs/agentq.md explains how
a tier is selected. A repository can pin a tier in its own policy.
Every tier must pair two different providers. A model does not review its
own implementation.

tiers.summary: normal engineering work, and the tier a task gets when no signal says otherwise
work that genuinely benefits from the strongest reasoning models

$comment: The transparent part of the classifier. Every rule below reads issue
metadata that a human wrote: the labels, and the title. A rule never
reads model output, and no rule calls a model to choose a model.
escalate.labels and escalate.words raise a task to escalate.tier. A word
matches on a word boundary in the lower-cased title.
byLabel maps the ordinary issue taxonomy onto a tier.
breadth.acceptanceCriteria.hard is the number of acceptance-criteria
items in the issue body that makes a task hard on scope alone.

escalate.summary: the task changes a security, authority, release or persistence boundary
